Sandbox_TraditionalPreservationFishMeat_: Days to salt dry in the best weather. Kentucky's weather makes it about 15 to 34.
The longest cold or damp weather can stretch salt drying, not counting rain.
Days to cold dry stockfish at the best temperature and wind. Kentucky's winter makes it about 50 to 55 when hung from late October to January; real stockfish takes about 90.
Days for stockfish to ripen in storage, on its own food clock. A Stockfish Pallet in a loft halves it. Real stockfish matures for 60 to 90.

Days for a dry cured cut (Beef (Dry Cured), Mutton (Cold Smoked) and the rest) to age after it has dried, on its own food clock. Left hanging where it dried, three quarters of that. Aged, it lifts the mood more.
Days for a Country Ham to age after it has dried, on its own food clock. Left hanging where it dried, three quarters of that. Real country hams age for six months to a year.

Days in the tub for a batch with a big fish (over 2.2 weight) or a half-weight cut of meat. Small fish take half as long, and sizes between are in between. The long country cure of meat keeps its 10 and 21 days.
How quickly the wrong season or the wrong cure spoils fish and meat: on a drying station, in the Salting Tub and in the Smokehouse. Off, nothing spoils while it cures or dries.
Pigs give Pork Fat, cattle Beef Suet and sheep Mutton Fat when butchered, most on a Butchering Hook. Two pieces render in a pot to one Lard or Tallow. Off, Lard is loot only, as in the base game.

An adult pig gives some of its Pork as whole Legs of Pork for country ham: five pieces make one leg, which keeps their food, so the pig's meat stays the same. One or two on a Butchering Hook, up to three from a big pig, usually none from the ground. Off, all Pork, as in the base game.
Beef, mutton, venison and pork can be packed in salt and cured in the Salting Tub: for charque, hot smoking, dry cured meat and country ham. Off, meat isn't salted.
Days to dry charque in hot sun (25 C and up) and a breeze. Kentucky's summer makes it about 7 to 11 under a roof; real charque takes 4 to 6.

A crock of Potted Meat keeps 120 days in a fridge or a cold month, about 110 in a winter basement and 64 in a summer one; a room follows the season, from as long as a fridge in winter to 14 days in summer (18 while the grid powers it); and the first portion taken costs a third of the time it has left. Off, it keeps 60 days anywhere, as plain food.
